chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Sa'd al-Askaf, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the pilgrim begins his preparation, he does not take a step with regards to something from his preparations, except that Allah Mighty and Majestic Writes ten good deeds for him, and Deletes ten sins from him, and Raises ten Levels for him, until he is free from his preparations. When he is free and he faces his ride with it, he does not place a shoe nor does he raise it, except that Allah Mighty and Majestic Writes for him similar to that until he has completed his rituals. So when he has completed his rituals, Allah Forgives his sins for him.'

And Dhu al-Hijjah, and Al-Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal are four months in which the good deeds are Written for him and the sins are not Written against him, except if he comes to a major sin. So when the four months are past, he is mixed with the people'.

key_terms.خُلِطَ بِالنَّاس: Mixed with the people (returning to normal state)
key_terms.مُوجِبَة: Major sin / Cause for recording sins

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and sins forgiveness for a Muslim during the Hajj preparation and journey?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the cumulative spiritual merit of Hajj, emphasizing that the intention and preparation phase are as significant as the rituals themselves, with rewards accruing for every step. It introduces the concept of 'Istiqra' (residence) in the sacred months, where a pilgrim who remains in a state of ritual purity and devotion enjoys a unique period where good deeds are recorded but minor sins are not, a state that ends upon rejoining the general populace. This underscores the Shia scholarly view of Hajj as a comprehensive spiritual journey beginning with the heart's intention and physical preparation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Sa’ad Al Askaf who said, 
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the pilgrim begins his preparation, he does not take a step with regards to something from his preparations, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Writes ten good deeds for him, and Deletes ten sin from him, and Raises ten Levels for him, until he is free from his preparations. When he is free and he faces his ride with it, he does not place a shoe nor does he raise it, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Writes for him similar to that until he has completed his rituals. So when he has completed his rituals, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives his sins for him.
And Zil-Hijja, and Al-Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabbi Al-Awwal are four months in which the good deeds are Written for him and the sins are not Written against him, except if he comes to a major sin. So when the four months are past, he is mixed with the people’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub from Sa‘d al-Iskaf who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘When a pilgrim (al-Hajj) prepares his supplies for Hajj, for every step that he walks for the preparation, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, writes down for him ten good deeds, deletes ten sins and raises for him ten degrees until his preparation is complete, whenever it happens. When his animal for transportation moves, for every step lifted up or placed on the ground Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, writes down for him the same number of good deeds until all of the acts of Hajj are complete, at which point Allah forgives his sins.

During the months of Dhu al-Hajj ah, al-Muharram, Safar, Rabi’ al-Awwal, which are four months, good deeds are written for him. No evil deed is written against him until he in fact commits one (a major sin). After these four months he is mixed with people.’”
